items.title: The Korean War never formally ended
items.claim: How did the Korean War conclude?

options.text: An armistice signed at Panmunjom on 27 July 1953 by representatives of the UN Command, North Korea and China — but no peace treaty; the Koreas remain technically at war and the DMZ at the 38th parallel divides them

items.reveal:
Armistice negotiations began in July 1951 and lasted two years, largely over the issue of prisoner repatriation. South Korean President Syngman Rhee refused to sign and unilaterally released 27,000 North Korean POWs in June 1953.

The Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) is 4 km wide and around 250 km long — one of the most heavily militarised borders in the world. Periodic incidents (the 1968 capture of USS Pueblo, the 2010 Yeonpyeong shelling) keep the conflict warm.

Moves toward a formal peace declaration have repeatedly stalled. The Korean War cost around 3 million lives — Korean civilians the majority — and shaped East Asian security for over 70 years.
items.why: Unresolved conflicts shape decades. The absence of a Korean peace treaty in 1953 is the structural foundation of every subsequent crisis on the peninsula.

items.title: McCarthy was censured by his own Senate in 1954
items.claim: How did Joseph McCarthy's anti-communist campaign end?

options.text: After televised Army-McCarthy hearings exposed his methods, the Senate voted 67-22 to censure him on 2 December 1954; he died of liver failure in 1957 aged 48
He resigned and joined the Republican Party leadership

items.reveal:
McCarthy had risen on a 1950 Wheeling speech claiming 205 communists in the State Department. The Army-McCarthy hearings (April-June 1954) were televised; Army counsel Joseph Welch's 'Have you no sense of decency, sir?' on 9 June became the iconic moment.

Edward R. Murrow's CBS broadcast 'See It Now' on 9 March 1954 had already turned mainstream opinion. The Senate censure vote followed in December.

HUAC (House Un-American Activities Committee), the Hollywood blacklist, loyalty oaths and the Smith Act prosecutions continued separately and outlasted McCarthy.
items.why: McCarthyism as a phenomenon was bigger than McCarthy. His fall did not end the Red Scare — but it ended one specific style of grandstanding accusation, and television was central to both his rise and fall.
